page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-32 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of memory. It runs on the Ampere Altra processor family using Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 3.0 GHz on the arm64 architecture. The CPU configuration provides 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB RAM per core. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, contains no bundled local storage, and does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced multi-core execution alongside typical Arm Neoverse-N1 single-thread limits. The instance records a multi-core Geekbench score of 9,720.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 28,406.08, falling in the middle 50% tier. In contrast, single-core metrics fall into the bottom 25%, characterized by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,112.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 23.29 GB/sec. Memory performance remains solid, achieving 130.22 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 67.39 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth for 256MB blocks, alongside 19.59 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 24.6 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs center around low single-core throughput and the complete lack of local NVMe storage, meaning block storage must be mounted separately across the network. However, because each vCPU corresponds directly to an unshared physical core, the configuration delivers predictable multi-threaded CPU utilization without hyperthreading contention. The high core-to-memory density offers strong operational cost efficiency for parallelized processing pools.

The VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-32 is well aligned with horizontally scalable multi-threaded workloads, including web serving, software compilation pipelines, continuous integration, container clusters, and distributed Redis caches that do not rely on local disk I/O.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-32 is a compute-focused Arm-based instance powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere Altra processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 32.0 GB of RAM. Operating on a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, it lacks local storage and GPU hardware, relying exclusively on remote block volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark data reflects average multi-core efficiency, logging 28,406.08 in stress-ng multi-core and 9,720.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, contrasted by lower single-threaded scores such as 1,112.0 in Geekbench single-core. Memory bandwidth is consistent, reaching 130.22 GB/sec for uncached reads, supporting 19.59 million Redis SET operations per second and 24.6 GB/sec static web throughput. Without hyperthreading contention, this profile provides cost-effective multi-threaded throughput for CI/CD builds, container runtimes, web serving fleets, and distributed key-value data layers.
